_about: Every GRPO reward function, keyed by name. Built-ins set reward_type to the name; gym entries set reward_type=gym and gym_verifier=<name>. Gym entries summarise NVIDIA NeMo Gym v0.7.0 (the version the gym image ships); doc links to the verifier's source and README. In row_fields, * marks fields the verifier's schema requires. general_purpose=false means it is tied to one benchmark's data format or a niche domain.

tool_call.summary: Checks that the model calls the target tool with the target arguments.
tool_call.reward: 1.0 right tool and arguments; 0.5 right tool, wrong arguments; 0 wrong or no call.
tool_call.answer_format: <tool_call>{"name": ..., "arguments": ...}</tool_call> or a bare {"name", "arguments"} JSON object; the chat template's tool format covers it, no system prompt needed.
tool_call.row_fields: question, tools (OpenAI function schemas), target_tool_name, target_arguments (object or JSON string). All required.
tool_call.good_for: single-turn tool calling: pick the right tool and fill its arguments
tool_call.caveats: Single-turn only; multi-turn messages traces are not supported. The model must support tools in its chat template.

math.summary: Reads the final answer from \boxed{} or <answer></answer> and compares it with the reference, exact or math-equivalent.
math.answer_format: \boxed{X}; the default system prompt already asks for it.
math.row_fields: A prompt column (text_column) and a reference-answer column (label_column).
math.good_for: math and any short checkable answer: numbers, expressions, single words, labels
math.caveats: Short answers only; free-form text or paraphrases score 0.

arc_agi.summary: Checks that the predicted ARC output grid (2-D integer list) exactly equals the expected grid.
arc_agi.answer_format: \boxed{[[1,2],[3,4]]}, integers only; unboxed, the first bare [[...]] is used (may be an echoed input). Needs a system prompt asking for the box.
arc_agi.row_fields: expected_output (needed), e.g. [[0,1],[1,0]]. train / test_input only build the prompt; task_id optional.
arc_agi.good_for: grid / matrix transformation puzzles with an exact integer-grid answer
arc_agi.caveats: Integer 2-D grids only. Schema requires nothing, so a row missing expected_output silently scores 0.

asr_with_pc.summary: Scores a speech transcript against a reference by word error rate, with punctuation and capitalization.
asr_with_pc.reward: Binary: 1 if WER(-PC) < 0.5 (or no hallucination for that task type).
asr_with_pc.row_fields: expected_answer (reference transcript); task_type ASR-PC | ASR | ASR_LEADERBOARD | Hallucination.
asr_with_pc.caveats: Audio input: needs an audio-capable model and audio in the request. Useless for text-only training.

assaybench.summary: Scores a ranked list of human gene symbols predicted as CRISPR-screen hits against graded relevance genes.
assaybench.answer_format: DSPy-style '[[ ## answer ## ]] GENE1, GENE2, ...' (comma-separated HGNC symbols). Needs a system prompt.
assaybench.good_for: ranking genes for a biology screen description
assaybench.caveats: Very niche domain and benchmark-specific metric.

bunsenbench_chemistry_mcq.summary: Lenient multiple-choice grader: extracts the chosen letter or exact option text and compares it with the gold choice.
bunsenbench_chemistry_mcq.answer_format: Very lenient: <answer> tags, \boxed{}, 'Answer: X', or a bare letter / option text. A short format hint is enough.
bunsenbench_chemistry_mcq.row_fields: options e.g. [{"A":"OH-"},{"B":"H2O"}] (or choices ["OH-","H2O"]); expected_answer e.g. "B" or the option text.
bunsenbench_chemistry_mcq.good_for: any multiple-choice task where the model may answer with the letter or the option text
bunsenbench_chemistry_mcq.caveats: Domain-agnostic despite the chemistry name. Option text must match exactly after normalization.

calendar.summary: Checks that a JSON schedule places exactly the expected events with no overlaps, each meeting its duration, window and before/after/between/at constraint.
calendar.reward: Binary 1/0; any violation, or a <think> tag in the reply, scores 0.
calendar.answer_format: JSON list of {event_id, event_name, start_time "HH:MM", duration}. Needs a system prompt describing it.
calendar.caveats: Built for multi-turn, but a single prompt listing all events works. Fixed constraint grammar. Thinking models must not emit <think> in the answer.

equivalence_rule.summary: Compares the whole reply with expected_answer after lowercasing and collapsing whitespace.
equivalence_rule.answer_format: The entire reply must be only the answer. Needs a system prompt saying 'output only the answer'.
equivalence_rule.good_for: short exact answers where the model outputs nothing but the answer
equivalence_rule.caveats: Very strict: any extra word scores 0. string_match is usually the better choice.

ether0.summary: Grades a chemistry answer (usually a SMILES molecule) with the ether0 eval function named in the row's solution string.
ether0.answer_format: <answer>SMILES</answer> (\boxed{} also works). Needs a system prompt.
ether0.good_for: molecule-generation / chemistry reasoning on ether0 data
ether0.caveats: Needs ether0's encoded solution strings. Very niche.

format_verification.summary: Checks format only: enough lines match given regexes, or all expected citation markers appear and no unexpected ones.
format_verification.answer_format: Free text in whatever format the prompt asks for (numbered lists, headings, [ref:N] citations, ...).
format_verification.good_for: teaching an output format or citation-marker style
format_verification.caveats: Rewards format only, so it can be satisfied with wrong content.

fukuyamabench.summary: Checks that a predicted multi-step organic reaction-mechanism pathway (SMILES steps) matches the gold pathway.
fukuyamabench.answer_format: JSON array of step objects (fenced ```json after '## Result'). Needs the upstream system prompt.
fukuyamabench.caveats: Benchmark-specific, expert-level; rewards will be very sparse.

generative_reward_model.summary: Trains a judge: the model scores two responses (1-5 each plus a ranking) per rubric and overall, rewarded for matching gold scores.
generative_reward_model.reward: Negative weighted L1 error, max 0; -100 on a parse failure.
generative_reward_model.answer_format: One JSON object {"rubric_evaluations":[...],"overall":{score_1,score_2,ranking}}. Needs a system prompt.
generative_reward_model.good_for: training a pairwise LLM-as-judge / reward model
generative_reward_model.caveats: Unbounded negative reward with a -100 cliff. Needs gold scores for response pairs.

gpqa_diamond.summary: Multiple-choice grader: extracts the final letter from \boxed{} or 'Answer: X' and compares it with the gold letter.
gpqa_diamond.answer_format: \boxed{C} or 'Answer: C' (last one wins). Needs a system prompt.
gpqa_diamond.row_fields: expected_answer e.g. "C"; options recommended e.g. [{"A":"..."},{"B":"..."}] to restrict valid letters.
gpqa_diamond.good_for: any multiple-choice task with letter answers, accepting 'Answer: X' as well as \boxed{}
gpqa_diamond.caveats: Generic despite the name. Letters only; option text is not matched.

graphwalks.summary: Compares the set of items in a final 'Final Answer: [a, b, c]' line with an expected set.
graphwalks.answer_format: Last non-empty line 'Final Answer: [item1, item2, ...]'. Needs a system prompt.
graphwalks.row_fields: expected_answer* JSON-list string e.g. "[\"n1\",\"n2\"]"; problem_type* (any tag).
graphwalks.good_for: tasks whose answer is an unordered set / list of short items
graphwalks.caveats: Items split on commas, so items can't contain commas; exact string match per item.

hotpotqa_qa.summary: Short-answer QA: checks the gold answer (or a surface variant) appears in the model's answer, with false-positive guards.
hotpotqa_qa.answer_format: Preferably JSON {"answer":"..."}; otherwise the whole reply. Keep it short.
hotpotqa_qa.good_for: free-form short factual answers with a known reference, tolerant of wording around the answer
hotpotqa_qa.caveats: Substring-based: suits short entities / numbers, not long-form. Hedged answers listing candidates may score.

iheval.summary: IHEval instruction-hierarchy benchmark: routes each row by task name to an upstream checker (F1, ROUGE-L, exact match, IFEval rules).
iheval.answer_format: Task-dependent; comes from the benchmark's prompts.
iheval.row_fields: task* (one of the 8 IHEval names), setting, answer (gold), instruction.
iheval.caveats: Benchmark-specific task names and gold structures.

imo_gradingbench.summary: Proof grading: the reply must end with correct / almost / partial / incorrect, matched against the gold grade.
imo_gradingbench.answer_format: Last word is correct, almost, partial or incorrect. Needs a system prompt.
imo_gradingbench.caveats: Label set hardcoded to these four words.

instruction_following.summary: Checks the reply against IFEval / IFBench-style verifiable constraints (word count, paragraphs, keywords, last word, format, ...).
instruction_following.reward: Binary 1/0 if all constraints pass; grading_mode fraction gives the fraction passed.
instruction_following.answer_format: Free text satisfying the constraints stated in the prompt.
instruction_following.good_for: open-ended prompts with checkable length / format / keyword constraints
instruction_following.caveats: Constraints must come from the IFEval registry with exact kwargs. Content quality is not judged.

lc_niah.summary: Set-F1 of a 'Final Answer: [..]' list against the expected list, penalised when the reasoning copies chunks of the prompt verbatim.
lc_niah.answer_format: Last line 'Final Answer: [a, b, ...]'. Needs a system prompt.
lc_niah.good_for: long-context retrieval of a set of items
lc_niah.caveats: The copy penalty only reads reasoning summaries; otherwise it behaves like graphwalks.

mcqa.summary: Multiple-choice grader: extracts the answer letter from the last \boxed{} and compares it with the gold letter.
mcqa.answer_format: \boxed{B}. The platform's default system prompt for mcqa already asks for it.
mcqa.caveats: Schema marks nothing required, but without options / expected_answer every row scores 0. An unboxed answer scores 0.

mrcr.summary: The reply must start with a given random prefix; then its similarity to the expected text is measured.
mrcr.reward: Continuous [0,1] SequenceMatcher ratio; 0 without the prefix.
mrcr.answer_format: random_string_to_prepend + the reproduced text, nothing before it.
mrcr.good_for: exact long-text recall from a long context
mrcr.caveats: Benchmark-shaped (multi-round coreference); character similarity rewards copying.

proof_genselect.summary: Pairwise selection: the model compares two candidate solutions and names the better one.
proof_genselect.answer_format: <best_solution>1</best_solution> or <best_solution>2</best_solution> after any reasoning. Needs a system prompt.
proof_genselect.row_fields: correct_index* (1 or 2); problem*, proof_1*, proof_2* (strings; the prompt must contain them too).
proof_genselect.good_for: pick-the-better-of-two tasks (solutions, answers, essays) with a known winner

ragtruth.summary: Hallucination detection: the model lists hallucinated spans as JSON; its yes/no verdict is compared with the gold label.
ragtruth.answer_format: One JSON object {"hallucination list": [...]}. Needs a system prompt.
ragtruth.good_for: detecting unsupported claims in a context-grounded answer
ragtruth.caveats: Unparseable output counts as 'no hallucination', so garbage scores 1 on is_halu=false rows: balance the labels and always set is_halu.

ruler.summary: Case-insensitive check that the reference strings appear anywhere in the reply (RULER long-context benchmark).
ruler.reward: Continuous: fraction of outputs found; subsets qa_1 / qa_2 score 1 if any is found.
ruler.answer_format: Free text containing the answer string(s).
ruler.row_fields: outputs* e.g. ["NRBQA","KMLJX"]; length* (int, unused); subset* e.g. "vt" or "qa_1".
ruler.good_for: answers that must mention all listed keywords / values
ruler.caveats: Easily gamed by long replies listing many candidates.

scicodepile.summary: Runs the Python function from the reply's last code block against the row's check(candidate) test.
scicodepile.reward: Binary 1/0: the test passes within 120 s.
scicodepile.answer_format: A complete Python function in a ```python block, named entry_point.
scicodepile.good_for: Python function-writing tasks with unit tests
scicodepile.caveats: Runs model code in a subprocess (memory limit only, not a sandbox). Libraries limited to the image.

spartqa.summary: Text-option choice: the 'Final answer:' must resolve to exactly one candidate phrase (or 'both of them' / 'none of them') matching the gold.
spartqa.answer_format: Ends with 'Final answer: <candidate copied verbatim>'. Needs a system prompt.
spartqa.row_fields: target e.g. "the red circle"; options recommended e.g. ["the red circle","the blue square"].
spartqa.caveats: Always adds 'both of them' / 'none of them' as valid labels.

string_match.summary: Extracts the final answer and compares it with the reference, normalising case, numbers, LaTeX, lists and units.
string_match.reward: 1.0 normalised match; 0.98 near-numeric match (~1% relative error); else 0.
string_match.answer_format: 'Final answer: X' / 'Answer: X', falling back to \boxed{X} (extraction_mode can switch to boxed, last_line, full_response). Needs a system prompt.
string_match.row_fields: expected_answer* e.g. "3.14" or "Paris"; extraction_mode, case_sensitive optional.
string_match.good_for: free-form short answers (text or numeric) with a known reference
string_match.caveats: Short canonical answers only; synonyms and paraphrases score 0.

structeval.summary: Checks the reply contains a parseable JSON / YAML / TOML / XML / CSV document with the required key paths.
structeval.reward: Partial credit [0,1]: 0.2 x parses + 0.8 x fraction of key paths present.
structeval.answer_format: A fenced code block with the document in output_type.
structeval.row_fields: output_type* json | yaml | toml | xml | csv; raw_output_metric* e.g. ["user.name","items[0].id"]; task_id*, task_name*, input_type* (metadata strings).
structeval.good_for: generating structured documents with required fields
structeval.caveats: Checks structure and key presence only, not values.

swe_pivot.summary: PivotRL for SWE agents: checks the model's tool call at a trajectory pivot matches the demonstrated call.
swe_pivot.answer_format: A Responses-API function_call item, not text.
swe_pivot.caveats: A text answer always scores 0; not usable with single-turn text GRPO.

terminal_multi_harness.summary: Next-step action verifier for agent harnesses: compares the model's message or tool call(s) with the expected action.
terminal_multi_harness.answer_format: Responses-API function_call item(s) matching declared tools; message rows accept any text.
terminal_multi_harness.row_fields: expected_action* {type: message | function_call | function_call_batch, ...}; harness, declared_tools optional.
terminal_multi_harness.caveats: With text answers the reward is trivial (message rows) or impossible (tool-call rows); not usable with single-turn text GRPO.
